verdict.rationale: PlayCanvas documents a first-party Editor API for programmatic scene manipulation and asset management. It also ships an official, npm-published Editor MCP Server that lets AI assistants modify project data in an open Editor session and verify the result. Together these cover the agent-driven editing core of the story, but nothing shows builds being triggered programmatically. A REST API is only listed as a plan feature, with no described capabilities. missing for 10: documented programmatic build/publish triggering, detail on node creation and property editing granularity, independent hands-on corroboration of agent-driven editing.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can drive the editor and project programmatically — create scenes and nodes, edit properties, trigger builds — through a documented scriptable interface

citations.quote: It allows developers to programmatically interact with the Editor, facilitating tasks such as scene manipulation, asset management, and custom tool integration.
The PlayCanvas Editor MCP Server connects AI assistants to an open PlayCanvas Editor session. It can modify project data and verify the result through the viewport or a running application.
change scenes from code with the Editor API, or from an agent with the MCP server.
